primary_source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999)

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999; Kew Muenchhusia crosswalk

traits.habit: Erect perennial wetland rose-mallow, genus key to 2.5 m
traits.leaves: Middle/upper leaves frequently hastate or arrowhead-based; stems, undersides and calyces glabrous or almost glabrous
traits.flowers: Pink or nearly white petals with dark crimson-purple basal blotch; petals 5–8 cm

records.diagnostic: Smooth calyx and stem, often arrowhead-shaped foliage separate from stellate-hairy Hibiscus/Muenchhusia moscheutos
holds: Old flora reports hybrids involving lasiocarpos in Dallas area; verify morphology in ambiguous specimens
No BONAP Hays range claim

records.historical: Hibiscus moscheutos L. subsp. lasiocarpos (Cav.) Blanch.; H. lasiocarpos Cav.
records.source: Diggs et al. 1999 and Kew POWO

traits.habit: Erect tall perennial to 2.5 m (species account)
traits.leaves: Lanceolate to ovate, some angled, up to 22 cm; long petioles to 10 cm; blade upper face permanently pubescent
traits.flowers: White to rosy petals with dark crimson-purple center; 5–10 cm (species account)
traits.habitat: Wet sites, east and southeast Texas extending westward in historical account

records.diagnostic: Persistent hairs on leaf upper face plus dense capsule pubescence distinguish from subsp. moscheutos; compare nearly smooth and hastate H. laevis
holds: Avoid genus/rank mismatch: Kew recognizes Muenchhusia moscheutos subsp. lasiocarpos
Old Dallas hybrid notes complicate photo-only diagnoses
BONAP target counties unchecked

records.historical: Hibiscus moscheutos L.; subsp. moscheutos at 1999 flora
records.source: Diggs et al. 1999 and Kew POWO

traits.leaves: Lanceolate to ovate, some angled or obscurely lobed, to 22 cm; subspecies moscheutos generally petioles to 5 cm and leaf upper surface glabrous or becoming so
traits.flowers: Petals 5–10 cm, white/cream-yellow with dark red-purple basal patch
traits.fruit: Glabrous capsule in the historical subspecies key
traits.habitat: Wetlands, especially eastern and southeastern Texas

records.diagnostic: Subspecies-level distinction: smooth capsule and upper-leaf face versus hairy fruit and upper blade in lasiocarpos
holds: Modern inventory species M. moscheutos contains subsp. lasiocarpos as concept, so species record and subspecies record intentionally overlap taxonomically, but they are distinct inventory entries
Current accepted species name verified by Kew
BONAP county status not asserted

traits.habit: Perennial herb to subshrub, erect or spreading (FNA)
traits.leaves: Narrow lanceolate often hastate leaves with toothed margins; distinguish from broader cordate P. lasiopetala
traits.flowers: Axillary, pale pink/rose/lavender petals with darker basal blotch; precise measurements await full source audit
traits.fruit: Schizocarp about 6 mm diameter with five spineless reticulate-costate mericarps around 4 mm each
traits.habitat: Naturalized ornamental introductions outside South American native range

records.diagnostic: Narrow spear-shaped sometimes hastate leaves, pale flower with darker center, awnless reticulate five-part fruit
holds: FNA indicates species native in South America, introduced in North America; no native Hays status
Original 1999 flora no species treatment found
Full FNA measurements incomplete

traits.habit: Small shrub around 1(–1.5) m; sparse to dense stellate stems
traits.leaves: Alternate, ovate-cordate, 2–5(–7.5) cm long, stellate hairy both sides
traits.flowers: Single axillary, 2–5 cm pedicel, involucel 5(–8) linear bracts, prominent green-veined calyx, rose-pink petals 12–25 mm; ten style branches, five carpels
traits.habitat: Rocky woodland Edwards Plateau and south Texas; planted landscapes farther north
traits.flowering: Growing season, individual flower typically one day

records.diagnostic: Broad cordate stellate leaves, deep pink petals and green-veined pointed calyx vs narrow hastate-leaf P. hastata
holds: Cultivated farther north does not establish county native occurrence
Flower duration observation from source; no invented hours

records.historical: Rhynchosida physocalyx (A.Gray) Fryxell; Sida physocalyx A.Gray

traits.habit: Perennial fleshy-woody rootstock; spreading/decumbent stems to 40 cm
traits.leaves: Stellate-hairy, suborbicular to oblong 6 × 5 cm maximum, cordate base, rounded apex
traits.flowers: Axillary solitary, calyx lobes cordate, mucronate, ca. 8 mm in flower, enlarging and enclosing fruit, yellow/buff petals roughly calyx length
traits.fruit: Disklike darkening schizocarp 10–14 carpels, inflated/enclosed by enlarged calyx
traits.flowering: April–October from continuation of species treatment

records.diagnostic: Inflated mature calyx and 10–14 mostly beakless carpels contrast with Sida, whose calyx does not fully inflate
holds: Flora historical synonym Sida physocalyx should not be indexed as distinct species
BONAP target range remains unverified

records.historical: Sida abutifolia Mill. (1999 flora orthographic name; modern inventory spelling abutilifolia needs nomenclatural check)

traits.habit: Woody-rooted perennial; prostrate stems to 50 cm
traits.leaves: Stellate pubescence, linear to ovate/oblong, up to 35 mm, crenate-dentate
traits.flowers: Axillary yellow petals much longer than 5 mm calyx; long pedicels relative to petioles
traits.fruit: Five dehiscent carpels, apiculate to two-pointed (generic Sida)
traits.habitat: Limestone outcrops and rocky prairie and roadsides

records.diagnostic: Prostrate, spineless under petiole, elongated pedicels vs erect prickly S. spinosa
holds: CRITICAL: 1999 spelling Sida abutifolia vs repo Sida abutilifolia; verify whether repo misspells accepted name. Do not silently rewrite species or treat as verified synonym
Original flora synonyms Sida filicaulis Torr. & A.Gray
BONAP target status unreviewed

traits.habit: Annual erect branched up to ca. 1 m, minutely stellate-pubescent
traits.leaves: Ovate to narrow lanceolate, to 55 × 30 mm, crenate-dentate
traits.flowers: Pale yellow axillary petals only slightly longer than calyx; calyx 5–7 mm
traits.fruit: Five carpels, each with two beaks
traits.habitat: Disturbed/waste sites, southeastern and eastern Texas west to East Cross Timbers

records.diagnostic: About 1-mm spine-like tubercle below petiole on mature leaves, pedicels shorter than petioles, erect growth contrasts with prostrate S. abutifolia
holds: Small petiolar spine may be missing in partial photograph; verify several nodes

traits.habit: Perennial usually erect/ascending western species; FNA genus key stems (2–)4–10 dm
traits.leaves: Frequently 3–5-lobed or pedately divided, pale green/gray-green stellate pubescence
traits.flowers: Typical globemallow corolla red-orange/pink depending populations; exact species petal measurements not sourced in this pass
traits.fruit: Mallow schizocarp divided into indehiscent basal and dehiscent distal portions; species mericarp counts require full treatment
traits.habitat: Intermountain West and southwestern states, not presumed native in Hays

records.diagnostic: Deeply lobed to pedately divided leaves and erect western globemallow habit vs mostly unlobed woolly coastal S. lindheimeri
holds: Not present as a named species in 1999 local flora; FNA genus key and species treatment used
County and accepted varietal concept pending; morphology partial

traits.habit: Perennial with decumbent white-hairy stems 20–70 cm
traits.leaves: White-silvery below and green above, deltate-ovate, unlobed or shallowly 3-lobed, to ca. 4 cm, cordate/truncate base, broadly crenate
traits.flowers: Dense racemes, usually nonleafy tip, sepals 8–15 mm, red or pink petals 15–25 mm; yellow anthers
traits.fruit: Hemispheric schizocarp, about 18 mericarps each 4 mm, distal dehiscent part 60–70% of segment; 2–3 seeds per mericarp
traits.habitat: Sandy soils, open thickets and roadsides, especially near Texas Gulf Coast

records.diagnostic: Very soft long pubescence, white/silver abaxial surfaces and decumbent growth; not diagnostic by flower color alone
holds: FNA notes species usually near coast, so native Hays status must not be inferred
Do not assume S. grossulariifolia and S. lindheimeri locally co-occur

records.historical: Tilia americana L. var. caroliniana (Mill.) Castigl.

traits.habit: Deciduous large tree up to about 30 m, young twigs tomentose
traits.leaves: Alternate ovate toothed to 13 cm, asymmetrical truncate/cordate base, underside sparse to dense stellate hairs, petiole to 35 mm
traits.flowers: Fragrant white/yellow, 5-merous, <=10 mm; long peduncle attached near middle of 12 × 3 cm straplike bract
traits.habitat: Low woods, eastern Texas; historical NE Texas records

records.diagnostic: Pendant flower/fruit cluster attached to central portion of long leaflike bract; unlike red mulberry asymmetrical leaf base and no lobes
holds: Historical var. caroliniana is NOT automatically equal to all species-wide Tilia americana populations; infraspecific concept review needed
Old family Tiliaceae now Malvaceae, preserve family routing and original source group
Do not certify Hays county from broad Edwards Plateau statement

policy: Research only. Preserve source pages, historical names, previous inventory, imagery and attribution. Do not turn holds into pass.
